agent_delegation.description: identity resolves a worker's delegation token (vxd_, minted per dispatch by agent-api) through /internal/validate, like an API key: signature, audience, expiry and the account still existing — so the gateway and flows authenticate a worker's tool calls without holding the delegation key themselves.
agent_delegation.when_unconfigured: /internal/validate answers 401 to every vxd_ bearer, so a worker's toolbelt is refused at the edge; API keys are unaffected. This is the no-agents profile, which mints no delegation tokens.

keys.description: shared internal secret the /internal/validate endpoint requires (fail-closed guard, main.py). Unset, gateway's validation hop 503s and every API-key check fails — so the boot refuses instead of coming up green and rejecting every call (the 2026-04-23 failure shape, #526). The same value gates /internal/bootstrap-admin and /internal/users/by-email, so a published placeholder is refused outright (F95).

keys.default: (unset — the admin surface then answers 500 'Admin authentication is not configured')
keys.description: admin bearer for the privileged admin surface (main.py:_admin_token → os.getenv, NO code default; every /admin route and the key-minting surface behind it). It read 'changeme' here, which described the deploy surfaces rather than the code — and that is exactly what a published default is: this token MINTS AN API KEY FOR ANY USER, so a stack left on the literal hands the whole account plane to anyone who read the repository. Same refusal INTERNAL_API_SECRET got in F95, for a strictly larger blast radius (A19). The list adds every default and example this repository has shipped for the admin key (compose's dev-admin-token, the chart's CHANGE_ME, the CI and test values, the old docs' placeholders); meeting-api's ADMIN_TOKEN and flows' VEXA_FLOWS_ADMIN_KEY refuse the same list (fact admin-token-placeholders).

PostgreSQL password for the users/tokens store. No default: it read 'postgres' here and in the code, a value published in this repository, so every stack nobody configured shared one database password anyone could read. Unset or a published literal refuses the boot, the same refusal compose's postgres service makes (deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml). Required even when DATABASE_URL overrides the URL.

explicit SQLAlchemy URL override; when unset the URL is built from the DB_* parts. Not set by any deploy surface (Lite parses a supplied URL into the DB_* parts instead); DB_PASSWORD is still required at boot when it is set.

SQLAlchemy async-engine pool_size (persistent connections per pod). Pure runtime override — reconcile with deploy/db-budget.json (Σ replicas × (pool_size + max_overflow) + reserved ≤ max_connections) on managed Postgres. #635.
SQLAlchemy async-engine max_overflow (burst connections above pool_size per pod). Pure runtime override — reconcile with deploy/db-budget.json. #635.

bounded initial-DB-connect retry: max attempts before failing loud. On a cold start where Postgres DNS isn't resolvable yet, the boot retries the first connect instead of exit(3)-ing into the k8s restart loop (#901). After this many attempts it re-raises.
bounded initial-DB-connect retry: base backoff seconds (capped-exponential: base×2^(n-1), clamped to DB_CONNECT_MAX_DELAY). #901.
bounded initial-DB-connect retry: max backoff seconds per attempt (the exponential is clamped here). #901.
dev conveniences toggle; does NOT relax the INTERNAL_API_SECRET requirement (a missing secret refuses boot even in dev — the 04-23 lesson).

keys.default: (empty — only existing users and admins may sign in, plus the holder of the admin claim code while nothing is configured and no admin has been claimed)
keys.description: The deployment's seed for the terminal sign-in allow-list (Vexa-ai/vexa#1783): comma-separated exact addresses and @domain entries, e.g. "@example.com,alice@example.org". A sign-in through any terminal door (emailed link, Google, Microsoft) is admitted only for an existing user, an admin, or an address on the effective list = these entries + the admin-edited `signin.allow` platform setting. A non-empty list also closes the unclaimed-instance door: only an address on it may sign in or claim the admin role. A malformed entry refuses the boot, naming the entry (app/signin_allow.py boot_problems). Read on every POST /internal/signin-admission and /internal/bootstrap-admin (app/signin_allow.py), so a change applies on restart with no migration. Removing an entry does not remove an account that already exists: existing users stay admitted.

keys.default: (empty — the first admin claims the role on the terminal's claim screen with the one-time code admin-api logs at boot)
keys.description: The instance's administrators, comma-separated exact addresses (no @domain entries: an admin is one person). Each is admitted to sign in, is an admin on /internal/validate and /internal/users/{id}/is-admin, and makes the instance count as having an admin, so the claim screen never shows, no admin claim code is issued, and nobody can claim the role. A malformed entry (not a full address, or an @domain) refuses the boot. Read here and nowhere else (app/signin_allow.py): the terminal holds no list of its own and only asks.

keys.default: (empty — no internal feed may be saved)
keys.description: operator allowance for calendar feeds served inside a private network (same value and grammar as meeting-api's, which fetches): exact host names and CIDRs. PUT /user/calendar and /user/calendars accept a feed URL whose literal address is inside a listed network or whose host is a listed name; every other internal URL is still a 422. An unsafe or malformed entry refuses the boot.

flows' intake, told that a person finished onboarding. IDENTITY TELLS FLOWS; IT DOES NOT ASK IT — the publish is best-effort, bounded at 2s and swallowed, so a deployment with no flows domain onboards people exactly as one with a flows domain does, and so does one where flows is simply down. Unset is therefore not a degraded state, it is a profile. The fact itself is stamped on the person in the same transaction as the account, so the record survives a publish that never lands (app/events.py, app/main.py POST /admin/users). Spelled bare FLOWS_API_URL until F208 — the only one of the three flows publishers not carrying the VEXA_ prefix this repo uses for its own keys; app/events.py still reads that name for one release, with a boot warning, so an unmigrated deployment keeps publishing.

operator key for the same edge, sent as X-Flows-Operator-Key (flows' POST /events is authenticated). The header was spelled X-Flows-Admin-Key until #1486 and flows still accepts that name for one release; admin-api sends only the new one. Declared as part of the edge rather than beside it: a publish target without its credential is a publish that always 401s, and the pair is what makes the edge real. Unset alongside an unset URL is the no-flows profile; unset with a URL set is a deployment whose facts are being refused, which is why both are visible on one declaration.

the HS256 key agent-api signs a worker's per-dispatch delegation token with; /internal/validate verifies vxd_ bearers with it. Same value as agent-api's VEXA_MCP_DELEGATION_SECRET; generated at install on every deploy surface. The placeholders and the key delegation.v1's published vectors are made with are refused at boot.

the service Redis, where agent-api revokes a worker's delegation token when its unit ends (vexa:delegation:revoked:<jti>, app/delegation_revocation.py), and where admin-api records each redeemed emailed sign-in link until it expires (vexa:signin-link:redeemed:<jti>, app/signin_links.py). /internal/validate reads it for every vxd_ bearer and refuses the token with 503 when it cannot, so an unreachable or wrong URL costs workers their toolbelt and never admits a revoked token; API keys never read it. /internal/signin-links/redeem answers 503 when it cannot write, and the terminal refuses that sign-in. On Lite the entrypoint's export reaches admin-api the way every supervisord program inherits it.
